Poushali Majumder

Helping young people build confidence, overcome barriers and access education, employment and training through mentoring, partnership working and community leadership.

My father is a social worker. I grew up watching him go into communities and give his time without hesitation. That shaped everything I became. Nearly a decade of documented youth and community work across India — now in London, ready to give everything to the young people of Tower Hamlets.

Based in E14, Tower Hamlets  |  First Class BSc (Hons)  |  Right to Work in UK
"Working for my society is something my heart has always wanted. I know I can give everything for this — because this is what makes me happy."
— Poushali Majumder

2013
National Integration Camp — West Tripura
Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) & District Administration, West Tripura
Participated in a residential national integration camp bringing together young people from across India, signed off by the District Magistrate and Collector of West Tripura.
2014 – 2015
State Youth Coordinator — Tripura
National Youth Project (NYP) / Bharat Ki Santaan
Coordinated and trained young people from Tripura to represent their state at national camps with hundreds of participants from across India and Sri Lanka. Prepared students in Tripura's culture, music, dance and language. Received Certificate of Appreciation for contribution to Linguistic National Integration.
2016

Represented Gomati District at the National Integration Camp. Achieved Certificate of Merit with 96% in Computer Skill Up-Gradation Training Programme, organised in collaboration with Vivekananda Kendra, Varanasi.
2017
Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat — District Level Declamation Contest
NYKS, Gomati District

Led Training on Youth Leadership and Community Development (TYLCD)
NYKS, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Govt. of India
Led a three-day residential training programme for young people on leadership, community engagement and personal development. Facilitated structured sessions for participants drawn from across the district — one of the most significant responsibilities in her youth work journey.

NYKS, Kamrup, Assam & Swastha Bharat Initiative, Tripura
Represented Tripura at the state-level camp in Assam, engaging with young people from multiple states. Also participated in village health camps providing community health awareness to rural populations in Tripura alongside medical teams, doctors and community leaders.

2023 — Present

Community and Professional Work — London

Moving to London in 2023 to study at the University of West London, Poushali continued her commitment to supporting others — as an International Student Ambassador, Peer Mentor and Course Representative. As a Peer Mentor, she managed an ongoing caseload of students, including those with ADHD and additional learning needs, conducting regular progress reviews, tracking outcomes against agreed goals and signposting to appropriate services where escalation was needed.

University of West London — careers and community event, supporting students from diverse backgrounds
Leadership skills and community engagement event at University of West London — bringing together students from diverse backgrounds to learn, connect and grow
UWL — peer mentoring students with ADHD and additional needs, providing one-to-one guidance, tracking progress, holding regular meetings and giving feedback to support academic achievement
Empowering Voices in Cybersecurity — UWL event bringing together students and professionals to champion diversity and inclusion in tech

Public Speaking

On Stage

TEDx Event — London

Confidence on a public stage is something Poushali has built over years — from leading sessions at national youth camps in India to presenting at events in London. Communication, presence and the ability to connect with an audience are at the heart of everything she does.

Why Tower Hamlets?

Living in Tower Hamlets, I see every day the diversity, resilience and potential of this community. I understand the barriers many young people face in accessing education, employment and training — and I know what a difference one trusted, informed person can make. I am not applying for this role because it seems like a good fit. I am applying because brokerage, tracking and person-centred youth support is the work I have always done, and Tower Hamlets is where I want to do it.
